case_title: BALKAR SINGH v. STATE OF HARYANA
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.27
neutral_facts: The deceased was the owner of a petrol pump and was killed during an altercation at a petrol pump. The deceased was accompanied by his brother and an employee when he visited another petrol pump. Four individuals, later identified as A-1 to A-4, approached the petrol pump and engaged in a confrontation. One of the individuals was armed with a knife and stabbed the deceased while another held him from behind. Two other individuals, armed with a gun and a danda, entered the office cabin and threatened witnesses. The deceased collapsed and the assailants fled. The FIR was registered the same day. The accused were arrested in the following days, and the case was handed over to the CBI. The trial court convicted several accused based on circumstantial evidence, but the High Court acquitted some of them. The Supreme Court reviewed the case and found that the prosecution failed to establish the conspiracy and murder charges against the accused.
